In this Review, we discuss advances in identifying, transferring and engineering plant immune receptors, with an emphasis on translational strategies that support sustainable agriculture. We further examine how tools such as CRISPR-based genome editing and AI-assisted protein design could progress this field. By integrating mechanistic insights with practical applications, we aim to engage bioengineers, plant scientists and agricultural biotechnologists in addressing the urgent need for environmentally sustainable crop production systems.

title: What it takes to commercialize a bone graft
abstract: Commercializing a bio-hybrid synthetic and xenogeneic bone graft requires integrated design that treats clinical and translational constraints as product requirements. Drawing on established components and validated concepts, we developed SmartBone as an effective composite solution. Here, we share key lessons from its commercialization, including systems engineering and the need for long-term performance evidence.

title: Fibre-architected intelligent permeable bioelectronics
abstract: Digital health-care technologies are used in medical practice for continuous monitoring, personalized diagnostics and targeted therapies. At the heart of these technologies are bioelectronics that interface biological systems with electronic platforms. However, conventional rigid and impermeable devices remain incompatible with soft, dynamic tissues, limiting long-term integration and clinical performance. Fibre-architected intelligent permeable bioelectronics, constructed from soft, porous and multiscale fibre networks, provide an emerging architectural approach to addressing these limitations. Featuring mechanical compliance, intrinsic permeability and multifunctionality (such as sensing, actuation and therapeutic delivery), these devices can operate reliably and over the long term in complex biological environments. This Review highlights key properties, smart materials and fabrication strategies of fibre-architected intelligent permeable bioelectronics. We further discuss how these bioelectronic technologies enable a range of digital health-care applications, categorized by sensing modality and clinical needs, including electrophysiology, biochemical detection, biomechanical monitoring and multimodal therapies. Furthermore, features, such as optical transparency and washability, are also discussed. Finally, we outline key challenges and translational strategies for integrating these bioelectronic systems into future personalized digital health-care ecosystems.

title: Anticipatory intelligence in clinical microbiology
abstract: Clinical microbiology needs an artificial intelligence system that predicts pathogen evolution and resistance to enable prevention. Laboratories should connect forecasts to confirmatory experiments and defined actions, then test them prospectively across time and populations, as well as govern false alarms, model updates and inequitable performance as carefully as diagnostic errors.

title: What closed-loop insulin delivery can — and cannot — teach us
abstract: Closed-loop insulin delivery is one of the great success stories of autonomous medicine. Its legacy, however, is not a universal blueprint, but the recognition that each closed-loop system must be designed around the biology, risks and lived realities of each condition.

title: Translation of in vivo CAR-T in China
abstract: China’s rapid progress in in vivo chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy reflects strengths of its biotechnology sector, which brings together research institutions, industry and hospitals to advance this emerging treatment. Drawing on our experience, we discuss how this expansion occurred and how speed and scale can be converted into original, clinically differentiated therapies.

title: Bioengineering strategies for prenatal therapy
abstract: Congenital and genetic disorders often cause death or lifelong disability, and treatments after birth are frequently unable to reverse the effects of established diseases. In utero therapies, which intervene during fetal development, offer an opportunity to treat conditions early, as demonstrated by existing fetal surgical therapies. Advances in bioengineering have expanded these approaches and improved their precision and potential effectiveness. However, challenges related to the safe delivery of therapies and the careful consideration of risks to both the mother and the fetus remain. In this Review, we examine emerging bioengineering strategies for fetal treatments, including tissue engineering, stem cell transplantation and gene-based approaches. We further discuss how these methods could overcome existing limitations and improve the translation of in utero therapies into clinical use.

title: Functional readouts of neural organoids
abstract: Human neural organoids have become powerful systems for investigating neural development, circuit formation and disease mechanisms in a species-specific context. Traditional animal models and two-dimensional cultures have long informed our understanding of neural activity, but they cannot reproduce the genetic, developmental and architectural complexity of the human brain. Neural organoids bridge this gap by enabling direct measurement of neuronal activity at cellular, ensemble and network scales. Functional interrogation now spans calcium and voltage imaging, patch clamp electrophysiology, and multielectrode array recordings, enabled by bioengineering advances that improve organoid viability and electrode–tissue coupling. Multi-regional assembloid models and xenotransplantation approaches further extend functional maturation and enable investigation of inter-regional connectivity. The integration of computational frameworks with functional measurements also enables extraction of quantitative features such as excitability, synchrony and network topology, linking molecular programs to emergent circuit behaviour. Furthermore, emerging studies demonstrate that neural organoids can exhibit synaptic plasticity, adaptive computation and goal-directed learning in closed-loop paradigms, opening research directions beyond spontaneous activity characterization. Functional organoids can also expand disease modelling by revealing mechanisms of network dysfunction across neurodevelopmental, neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. Nevertheless, the absence of standardized benchmarks, reference datasets and reproducible analysis pipelines continues to limit comparability across studies. This Review synthesizes current technologies and analytical strategies for probing activity in neural organoids; evaluates their translational relevance and limitations; and discusses how interdisciplinary integration of stem cell biology, bioengineering, systems neuroscience and computational modelling could establish robust frameworks for mechanistic and ethically grounded exploration of human brain function.

title: Digital cell factories for biomanufacturing
abstract: Metabolism-centric digital cell factories offer a pragmatic route to biomanufacturing optimization by emphasizing predictions of production performance and economic outcomes over biological detail.
